object_description: four triangular point buildings with mushroom-shaped ground floors
design_condition: Four freely arranged triangular buildings and striking trees create north-south cross-references between the city center and the future parking-garage entrance.

positive.statement: The analysis leads to a rhythmic arrangement of point buildings and striking trees that makes the Reuss more tangible.
The requirements for trains and buses are well managed in principle.
The access to the parking garage is very well done.
The trees are placed well and divide the street space effectively.
The trees also have enough space according to the cut solution.
The apartments have plenty of daylight and good views.
The apartment floor plans are attractive from a market perspective.
The expression and materialization correspond to and strengthen the project idea.
The detailed project offers conclusive suggestions in floor-plan layout and access issues.

negative.statement: It is unclear where the settlement begins and ends, or whether one more or one fewer building would be possible.
The random arrangement of serving areas and rooms has no spatial potential.
The underground parking is poorly implemented and the bicycle parking quality is unconvincing.
The residential primacy means the proposal contains too much settlement and too little station.
The buildings have limited scope for future development because of their hard bone.
The ground-floor entrance serves the overall system rather than the specific requirement.
The commercial areas are strongly determined by the concept of individual buildings.
The copper facade would probably have to be replaced for ecological reasons.
The radical body-and-tree concept does not do justice to the diverse requirements of the task and space.
The ground-floor uses suffer from the concept of individual volumes.
